topic: What antenna design considerations optimize ground station visibility during short service windows in LEO constellations?
consensus_response: To optimize ground station visibility, phased array antennas with circularly symmetric geometry can minimize interference and maximize signal gain. Atmospheric Phase Screen (APS) effects significantly impact signal strength and beam steering accuracy. Implementing Adaptive Beamforming (ABF) can help mitigate APS effects by dynamically adjusting the antenna's radiation pattern based on real-time satellite position and visibility. The Nakagami parameter (m) in the Line-of-Sight Shadowed-Rician (SR) fading model can be used to optimize the array factor and minimize signal loss.
reference_context: Low Earth Orbit constellations require a high level of system redundancy for coverage zones, with 60-70 satellites equally spaced in ascending nodes covering the whole surface of the earth. The time of satellite flight over a subscriber ranges from 10 minutes to 20 minutes.
